description: SPI idle-state pulls at the module: SCLK and MOSI (cable side), SCLK_DAC, DIN and SYNC (DAC side)
notes: FIVE OF THE MODULE'S SIX SPI PULLS - the sixth, CS_MOD's cable-side pull, is its own row, R-CS-PULL-MOD, because it is 100k and not 10k, and it has a partner at the instrument end, R-CS-PULL-INST (spi-link.md, 'CS_MOD's two pulls'). BOTH SIDES of the 74AHCT125. Cable side: SCLK and MOSI to DIG_GND, so the buffer's inputs do not float and crowbar when the instrument is absent. DAC side: SCLK_DAC and DIN down, SYNC up. They were bought for a buffer whose OE could be disabled; its OE is now tied on and its VCC is the DAC's own rail, so they matter only if the buffer fails with its outputs open. Kept as insurance on the one failure that latches (spi-link.md, 'Pulls on both sides of the buffer'). Module-alive-instrument-off is the normal state, not a fault; a stray CS edge latches garbage into the pitch DAC. DAC-SIDE SYNC PULLS TO AVDD (U-REG-DAC's rail, dac-rail), a pull-up on its consumer's rail: on any other rail a reversed ribbon could reach the DAC's SYNC pin and turn a $0.30 buffer failure into a DAC failure. UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F1002T5E, LCSC C17414

description: CS_MOD's cable-side pull-up at the module, to LOGIC_5V
notes: THE WEAK HALF OF CS_MOD'S TWO PULLS (the strong half is R-CS-PULL-INST at the instrument). On module-main as R-PULL-CS, from CS_MOD to LOGIC_5V - the rail of the part it holds, U-RX-MOD, whose first Schmitt gate it reaches through R-RX-CS (the 74AHCT125 behind it is on DAC_AVDD). 100k, NOT 10k: with the instrument plugged in and switched off, its 3V3 is dead, and 10k to 5V would push ~430uA through the ESP32's input clamp with the node stuck near 0.7V; 100k against R-CS-PULL-INST's 10k puts ~45uA into the dead rail and the node at ~0.45V, 50mV under U-RX-MOD's lowest V_T- of 0.5V [ds SN74AHCT14.pdf p.5] - so SYNC may read either way in that state, and either is harmless (spi-link.md, 'CS_MOD's two pulls'). With nothing plugged in it holds the receiver's input within 0.1V of 5V (1uA max input current [ds SN74AHCT14.pdf p.5]), so SYNC sits high and the DAC ignores SCLK. A PULL-DOWN HERE IS WRONG: the receive path does not invert (U-RX-MOD inverts twice), so it would hold SYNC low - selected - with the umbilical out. The arithmetic for all four link states is on spi-link.md, not restated here. UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F1003T5E, LCSC C149504

description: CS_MOD's pull-up at the instrument end, IO34 to the dev board's 3V3
notes: THE STRONG HALF OF CS_MOD'S TWO PULLS, on the main board (carrier/carrier's sheet) because 3V3 exists only at the instrument: from IO34 to DEV_3V3, beside J-MCU pins 14 and 13, on the MCU side of R-SPI-SER-CS so the source termination is untouched. IT IS WHAT HOLDS CS DESELECTED WHILE THE ESP32 RESETS AND BOOTS: GPIO34 has no pull at reset, input-enabled only [ds ESP32-S3-datasheet-v2.2.pdf p.17], and it is not a strapping pin (GPIO0, 3, 45, 46 [p.26]), so a pull here changes no boot mode. With R-CS-PULL-MOD's 100k to 5V in parallel the idle node is ~3.45V, which the ESP32's pad clamp holds to within ~17uA [calc on spi-link.md]. UNI-ROYAL 0805W8F1002T5E, LCSC C17414

description: Series termination on SCLK, MOSI and CS at the driving end
notes: THREE, 82R (owner, 2026-09-30: cs-fall-reentry, interfaces/spi-link/sim). *** 2m OF CAT5 IS A 100-OHM TRANSMISSION LINE (20ns round trip against 2-5ns edges), NOT AN RC CORNER *** - do not derive this from a corner frequency. *** U-TVS-SPI SITS ON THE PAD SIDE OF THESE, NOT THE CABLE SIDE: *** at J-UMB its 30 pF sends CS_MOD's returning edge back up through the far end's V_IL. The value is spi-series-r, derived on spi-link.md. FAULT CURRENT into a conductor shorted to ground: 3.3V / (82 + 17) = 33mA at the pad's strongest drive setting [calc]. The 40mA beside it on the datasheet is the TYPICAL drive at that setting (Table 5-4), not a limit; the absolute maximum table gives only 1500mA cumulative [ds ESP32-S3-datasheet-v2.2.pdf p.64-65]. 1206, 1/4 W: 33mA through 82R is 90mW, 36% of rating [calc; ds UNIROYAL-THICK-FILM-CHIP-RESISTOR-0805W8F.pdf, 1206 = 1/4 W, 200 V]. UNI-ROYAL 1206W4F820JT5E, LCSC C17980

description: ESD protection on the umbilical's SPI lines
notes: SCLK, MOSI, CS (+ one spare channel) to PWR_GND. ORDER CODE IS SP0504BAHTG AND IT IS SOT-23-5, NOT SOT-23-6 [SP0504BAHT.pdf p.1 ordering table, package outlines pp.6-7]; SP0505BAHTG is the SOT-23-6 part and brings a fifth channel if one is wanted. *** THE PART HAS NO PULSE RATING AT ALL. *** Eight pages carry no I_PP, no 8/20us or 10/1000us waveform, no surge curve and no theta-JA: it is ESD-rated only (IEC 61000-4-2, 20kV contact / 30kV air). What it does specify is a steady-state ceiling - package dissipation 0.225 W [Abs Max p.2, corroborated 'PD@70degC .225W' p.7]. SO A SUSTAINED FAULT IS NOT SURVIVED BY A BIGGER ARRAY; the fix is a series resistor or a resettable element. ALL FOUR CHANNELS SHARE ONE COMMON PIN (pin 2), to PWR_GND. *** ON THE PAD SIDE OF R-SPI-SER *** (IO34, IO35, IO36), close to J-UMB: on the cable side its capacitance reflects CS_MOD's returning edge back through the module's V_IL (cs-fall-reentry, interfaces/spi-link/sim), and there R-SPI-SER now limits what a sustained fault on a conductor pushes into it. U-TVS-CHAIN is a second package because it clamps at the J-CHAIN, elsewhere on the main board. THE ARRAY IS EFFECTIVELY UNI-DIRECTIONAL: the -0.8V negative clamp is a forward diode drop, not an avalanche knee. Fine for 0-3.3V SPI; MUST NOT be reused on a bipolar CV node. 30 pF per channel is high for a modern array; on the pad side it loads the pad, not the line, and interfaces/spi-link/sim carries it. DO NOT RE-PROPOSE onsemi ESD7104: it is a clean 4-channel 5V array on paper and ships only in UDFN10 and WDFNW10, leadless fine pitch, banned by the ADR 0013 package policy - as was SP3012-06UTG before it. Two parts have now been rejected for that one reason

description: The instrument's umbilical connector: etherCON A-series, vertical PCB mount, soldered to the umbilical adapter behind the tail cap
package: vertical PCB mount, THT: 8 contacts d0.8, G d1.2, 4 x d1.7 pegs, one 6.6 x 2 slot
notes: READ OFF THE BANKED DRAWING ST-NE8FAV rev B (datasheets/connectors/NEUTRIK-NE8FAV-DRAWING.pdf) and its data sheet. REAR MOUNTING, PANEL 3mm MAX [ds: 'Panel thickness max. 3 mm']: the oak tail cap is thicker, so it carries a recess from outside that leaves 3mm where the flange clamps - config/body.yaml ethercon.panel_max, mechanical/drc.echo 'tail cap recess for the etherCON inside the tail face'. Cutout (rear side): bore d22 min, two d3.2 min holes diagonally at 19.8 +/-0.1 x 19.8 +/-0.1. Flange 25 x 25, the axis 12.5 above its lower edge. The PCB's front face is 18.3 behind the flange's front face. LATCH UP: the PUSH tab on top, in the recess; the contacts above the axis, G below. CUT ITS TWO LOCATING PEGS OFF FLUSH before fitting: they stand below the flange and would go into the oak bottom (config/body.yaml ethercon.peg_below). FOOTPRINT (PCB layout, seen from the connector's back): contacts d0.8 on 2.54 in two rows 2.54 apart, staggered 1.27; G d1.2; four d1.7 pegs 16.85 apart; a 6.6 x 2 slot, R1. Mounted with Neutrik's A-series screws [ds: 'Mounting A-Screw'] - MECH-ETHERCON-SCREW. Ratings [ds]: 1.5A per contact, <=57V, 1kVdc, >1000 mating cycles, contacts 0.2um Au over Ni. MATES WITH 'NE8MC* or any standard RJ45 plug' [ds]; does NOT intermate with NE8MC6-MO or NKE6S* cables [ds]. NE8MX is not named - J-UMBILICAL-CABLE

part: 8-way 2.54mm right-angle pin header, single row, through-hole
description: Joins the umbilical adapter (PCB-UMB-ADAPTER) to the main board's tongue: soldered into both, no mated contacts
notes: PINOUT IS umbilical-pinmap, PIN N = etherCON PIN N: the adapter runs each of J-UMBILICAL-INST's pins straight to the same-numbered pin here, so 'J-UMB pin N' on any page is the same conductor as J-UMBILICAL pin N. FITTED: the insulator on the tongue, the 3.00 mm tails down through the tongue, the 6.00 mm posts through the adapter from its rear face [ds HANXIA-HX-PZ2.54-1x8P-WZ.pdf]; solder both, then trim the posts that stand in front of the adapter. The row meets the adapter between the etherCON's G tab and its peg line - mechanical/drc.echo 'J-UMB's row lands on the adapter clear of the etherCON's footprint'. RATING: one pin carries +12V (umbilical-current) and one PWR_GND; rate them above the module's current-limit trip (R-ILIM, hardware/module/umbilical-load-switch/), not the typical draw - the worst case is an overload just under the trip, carried indefinitely. The header's pins are rated 3 A [ds HANXIA-HX-PZ2.54-1x8P-WZ.pdf], above the etherCON's own 1.5A per contact [ds], which is the limit here. D-REVSHUNT and U-TVS-SPI sit at it. PIN 8 (DIG_GND) TIES TO THE MAIN BOARD'S GROUND (PWR_GND) AT THIS HEADER (ADR 0018): a short, wide connection at the pin. Route SCLK, MOSI and CS_MOD from the MCU side of J-MCU to here over unbroken ground, and keep AGND_SENSE (pin 2) off this return. The module end is dig-gnd-topology. hanxia HX PZ2.54-1x8P WZ (LCSC C32713267), hand-soldered: its insulator and row height are config/body.yaml boards.umb_joint_*. Samtec TSW-108-08-G-S-RA fits too (tail 2.29 [ds SAMTEC-TSW-HTSW-2.54MM-HEADER.pdf p.2])

description: Carries J-UMBILICAL-INST behind the tail cap and joins it to the main board by J-UMB
